title: Prove a sharp block-four direction-weight obstruction (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with an exact finite certificate. At block four, every correct width-five program in the declared shift/diagonal/coordinate-permutation game obeys

```text
Target leakage demand:       448 per array
Direction-v call leakage:   112 wt(v), exactly
Therefore:                  sum wt(v) >= 4 W
Coordinate calls only:      minimum 4 W, attained
```

Arbitrary complex register mixing, zero scratch, copies, erasures and arbitrary diagonal phases are allowed. Inverse calls have the same weight. General XOR-linear address maps are excluded. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

The new fifth-exterior-power face space has dimension 448 inside dimension 4368. Its target leakage Gram is exactly `(15/16) I_448`. The direction-weight ranks are 112, 224, 336 and 448. This also settles the obvious certificate's limitation: if every nonzero direction has unit price, its demand-to-cap ratio is exactly one. A better unrestricted-direction obstruction needs a changed certificate.

Credit Jacob Alan Sussman's #4628 for the kept-subspace and block-three face methods, and eumemic #288 and Swapnil Jain's P1/P2 as credited there. The new proof and checker are self-contained; no predecessor executable or reported rank was audited. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

## Evidence

Before this contribution, #4628 supplied the block-three face certificate and separate block-four bounds in other games. The new block-four certificate checks every one of 200,704 target-compression minors over the integers, all fifteen nonzero call directions over Gaussian integers with modular rank lower bounds and analytic upper bounds, and nine rejection controls. Both registered modes print `PASS_BLOCK4_COORDINATE_FACE_TARIFF`, and the runner prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/block4-coordinate-face-tariff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/block4-coordinate-face-tariff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/block4-coordinate-face-tariff
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/block4-coordinate-face-tariff --check-source-history
```

CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only. The direct ordinary and optimized checks each take about two seconds; registered replay takes about four seconds total. The exact committed-byte/source-history check passes for all five files. A read-only, Git-free committed export passes optimized isolated replay and preserves every exported byte. Its scientific output equals the generated hash-bound publication receipt.

The historical card baseline stopped with `KeyError: 'complex_profile'`; current baseline orientation stopped at sparse-omitted `research/fresh-helper-thinned/PROOF.md`. Neither is a new package failure or claimed successful replay. The package has no live external mathematical inputs. Canonical main was refreshed unchanged at `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43` before publication. The overlap helper covered 367 open PR bodies and 3,823 Discussion records; sparse local-note coverage was incomplete, supplemented by distinctive searches across main and merged PRs.

## Limitations

The program theorem is a written scoped proof supported by the exact finite identities. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The finite ranks concern block four only. This does not exclude unrestricted-direction small units, supply a physical implementation, price compilation, settle rounding, or prove a complete multiplication theorem. Those obligations were not run or claimed.

## Related open work

- #4628 studies small-unit lower bounds and supplies the predecessor method. This adds a new block-four certificate and a different weighted game, without rechecking its bounds.
- #4818 proposes a finite block-four three-array schedule. The present theorem concerns the stated width-five free-step contract, so it does not test that schedule or compare its observation ranks.
- #4819 proposes a finite block-four thirteen-array schedule. The same contract distinction applies; no schedule or paid-word audit is performed here.
- #4826 studies a block-five schedule, outside this block-four certificate.
- #4841 supplies phase-exact native compilation and contact-neighborhood results. Native admission and general address maps are outside this theorem.
- #4842 studies complete observation-matrix conditioning and paid-word admission for the proposed schedules. Its matrices and numerical norms are separate from the exterior-face leakage operators here.

The pre-DONE refresh inspected all nine other open submissions from this account created since the advance CLAIM: #4844, #4845, #4846, #4847, #4849, #4850, #4851, #4852 and #4854. They concern different objects from block-four exterior-face leakage; no new same-object numerical comparison is made.

## Open next questions

- Find a kept space with demand/cap above 7/2 for unit-priced arbitrary directions and diagonal phases. Test a weight-four call first; this space cannot supply that bound.
- Determine whether coordinate-face compression yields useful weighted bounds at another block size. Begin with the exact compression Gram; no new-block rank is claimed here.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed on exact head `8b8de0281f429b592932b424987cea3be178b213` in [run 39861300537](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39861300537): plan and registered package replay. The replay runs both warning-strict ordinary and optimized commands. Local registered replay, publication-byte/source-history checks and the read-only Git-free export also passed. Hosted execution is bounded automated verification, not independent human or formal proof-kernel acceptance.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: one isolated research package. The five added files contain the proof, verifier and metadata.
